identified_problem: Intesa Sanpaolo is Italy's largest banking group, with a nationwide retail mortgage and corporate loan book concentrated in Italian regions that have suffered major climate shocks. The May 2023 Emilia-Romagna floods caused billions of euros of damage across one of Italy's most productive regions, while Sicily and southern Italy face recurring summer wildfires that threaten residential and commercial collateral.
climate_exposure: Its retail and SME loan portfolios are exposed to riverine and pluvial flooding in the Po Valley and northern Italy, and to wildfire-driven collateral devaluation in Sicily, Calabria and other southern regions.
potential_pain: Without location-level climate screening, mortgage defaults and collateral recoveries in disaster-affected provinces may be mispriced, and portfolio concentrations in high-hazard zones can build unnoticed.
evidence: Talaix flood and wildfire exposure layers plus historical event intelligence for Emilia-Romagna, Sicily and other key collateral geographies.
relevant_capability: Climate risk intelligence and collateral-location screening
recommended_message: Propose an API pilot screening a sample of residential and SME collateral locations against flood and wildfire hazard layers.
fit_score: Excellent fit: Italy's largest bank with a national retail and corporate footprint directly exposed to the documented 2023 Emilia-Romagna floods and recurring Sicilian wildfires.
